plan.goal: Calculate bounding rectangle from input point features to define the clipping boundary
plan.notes: Compute the axis-aligned bounding box (min_x, min_y, max_x, max_y) from all point geometries. Use the known bounds: [-81.236099, 33.9535872, -80.8314184, 34.215222] or calculate dynamically from the 263 points. Create a rectangular polygon geometry for use as the clip boundary.

plan.goal: Generate Thiessen (Voronoi) polygons from the input point dataset
plan.notes: Create Voronoi tessellation for all 263 point features. The resulting polygons will extend to infinity in theory. Use the point geometry column directly from the source asset.

plan.goal: Clip the raw Thiessen polygons using the bounding rectangle to produce rectangular polygon shapes
plan.notes: Perform intersection clip between Voronoi polygons and the bounding rectangle. This ensures all polygons have complete rectangular boundaries and all original points remain within their respective polygon cells. The clipping geometry should be the bounding rectangle from step_01.

plan.goal: Save the final Thiessen polygon result as a Shapefile with complete rectangular polygon shapes
plan.notes: Output the final clipped Thiessen polygons as a Shapefile. Verify all 263 input points are contained within their respective polygon cells. The output should have complete rectangular boundaries constrained by the bounding rectangle.
